transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Samira Velasquez (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (CTO - Stratus), Priya Rao (Head of Security), Marcus Li (Infra)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot checkpoint focusing on security/compliance blockers, review of early perf results from the last 48 hours, and next steps for log retention and SSO test. Agreed to share logs and SOC2 scoping doc; customer to validate retention policy and SIEM ingestion.

Topics:
- Recent latency/cost results on the hosted pilot instances
- SSO/SAML integration status and test users
- Audit logs: format, retention, and forwarding to customer SIEM
- Data retention policy during pilot and after POC
- SOC2 readiness questions and responsibility split

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, appreciate it. we should be able to keep this tight 30 to 40 minutes, week three checkin for the stratus poc.
[00:12] Alex: yeah thanks jordan. short agenda from our side - we want to confirm the security items and review the numbers samira sent last night.
[00:19] Samira: great, i put together a trimmed set of logs and a per-model latency/cost csv, i can walk through the highlights.
[00:28] Priya: before we dive, just flagging two blockers - SSO metadata and how long logs are retained in your hosted offering, and whether those logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[00:40] Jordan: absolutely - those are on the list. quick primer: for the hosted pilot we persist request/response metadata for 30 days by default, payload redaction is on for downstream storage, and we offer log-forwarding via syslog or simple HTTP ingestion to a customer's SIEM.
[01:02] Marcus: when you say payload redaction, is that automatic redaction or configurable? we have sensitive pii in some prompts so we need control.
[01:11] Samira: it's configurable. by default we redact obvious patterns (emails, ssns, cc numbers) but you can opt-in to full payload redact, or we can provide hashing-only for traceability. note: full redact reduces some debugging signal.
[01:28] Priya: ok, good. also SOC2 — do you have any SOC2 attestations or a timeline? we saw a note in the onboarding portal but need more detail.
[01:38] Jordan: we're SOC2 Type II in flight — our attestation is scheduled for q4 2026. meanwhile we share a SOC2 readiness package, controls mapping, and audit logs samples. i'll send that after the call.
[01:52] Alex: thanks. samira can you summarize the perf numbers? the csv showed some spikes during larger batch runs.
[02:01] Samira: yeah so quick take — we've been running the tiled prompt workload on the 8k sequence hosted variant; median latency for single-turn requests is about 125ms, 95th at~580ms during peak. cost per 1k tokens is roughly $0.68 under current default batching. note: we saw a 20% tail latency increase when we enabled aggressive batching to save cost.
[02:28] Marcus: that's interesting — what's the batching policy right now, and is there an easy knob to tune for us to keep p95 below 500ms?
[02:36] Samira: current policy is dynamic batching with a 40ms hold window. we can lower to 20ms which will drop p95 by ~15% but increase token cost by around 12%. we provided the tradeoff table in the csv.
[02:55] Alex: okay so tradeoff accepted maybe for low-latency endpoints. which model variant were these runs on?
[03:03] Samira: these were on redwood-8k-v1 quantized 4-bit variant; dedicated variants would be a different profile.
[03:11] Priya: back to security — SSO. we attempted to upload SAML metadata earlier but our IdP wants a certificate thumbprint and a metadata URL. do you support metadata URL hosting?
[03:23] Jordan: yes, we host a metadata endpoint you can pull or we can ingest your metadata file directly. we also support idp-initiated and sp-initiated flows. for test we prefer you create a test user in your IdP and provide saml metadata and an sp-initiated login URL.
[03:42] Marcus: any chance to do a live SSO test this week? i can spin up a test user in the next 24 hours.
[03:47] Samira: that'd be ideal. we can coordinate; i can walk through SAML assertions and show roles mapping.
[03:54] Priya: and RBAC — we need to map roles so only select users can pull raw logs. is role mapping supported?
[04:02] Jordan: yep. RBAC is supported via groups from SAML or SCIM sync; we can map to console permissions and to API keys restrictions.
[04:12] Alex: on logs — format question: do we send full request/response or metadata-only? and sample size — samira's logs include full text which i don't want in our SIEM.
[04:24] Samira: you can choose the level: metadata-only (timings, tokens, model id), redacted payload (with tokens masked), or full with consent. for SIEM forwarding we recommend metadata-only with a hash of the prompt for dedupe.
[04:41] Marcus: can we also get structured audit events? our SIEM expects JSON fields like user_id, request_id, latency_ms, model_name.
[04:51] Samira: yes we have a structured JSON audit format; i'll attach the schema. note: in the export the field names might be slightly different in the pilot logs - red wood internal naming sometimes shows as model_ver or model_tag, transcription may show k v cache as K V cash, apologies.
[05:14] Priya: good heads up. about retention, jordan said 30 days default — can we set a 7-day retention for pilot? we have policy constraints.
[05:23] Jordan: yes, pilot-level retention policies can be shortened. we can do 7 days for logs and 0 days for request payloads, or you can set a custom window.
[05:33] Alex: perfect. will there be a cost delta for shorter retention?
[05:38] Samira: negligible for pilot, since storage footprint is tiny. if you move to production with audit logs retention beyond 90 days there are storage fees, we can model that.
[05:50] Marcus: a question on key management — if we go dedicated or private do we have KMS integration for encrypt at rest?
[05:58] Jordan: yes, for private deployments we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and bring-your-own-key. for hosted there's a managed key by default, and an option for KMS integration on enterprise contract.
[06:11] Priya: are audit logs tamper-evident? we want an append-only mechanism or signed logs.
[06:18] Samira: we do cryptographic checksums on log batches and can provide signed export bundles for audit. for compliance customers we recommend forwarding to their SIEM with immutability policies applied.
[06:31] Alex: ok, moving to results — any notable errors or quality regressions in the last 48 hours we should be aware of?
[06:39] Samira: we saw a small regression on one eval set after quantization, mostly around rare tokenization edge cases. we've flagged those examples and added a fallback to a slightly higher-precision variant for those routes.
[06:55] Marcus: did that fallback change the cost calc?
[06:59] Samira: marginally, about 3% effective increase for the affected calls, but it's limited to ~0.7% of traffic in your pilot so far.
[07:10] Priya: for the SOC2 pack — can you map out shared responsibility? we need to know what we must audit and what redwood operates.
[07:18] Jordan: yes, the SOC2 readiness doc has a simple matrix: control owner columns. i'll annotate which controls are customer-responsibility (identity, data classification) and which are vendor (runtime, physical security, patching).
[07:31] Alex: thanks. can you also include an itemized list of what logs we'll have access to versus what redwood retains?
[07:38] Jordan: will do. to be clear: you get tenant-scoped audit logs and can request ad-hoc exports; we retain a fuller set for a configurable period but can contractually limit that.
[07:52] Marcus: about SIEM ingestion — what's the throughput? we might want to forward tens of thousands of events a day.
[07:59] Samira: we support high-volume ingestion; typical pilot volumes we tested at up to 100k events/day via HTTP ingestion with batching and retries. we'll provide a sample ingestion playbook.
[08:13] Priya: can we have encryption in transit guaranteed? TLS mutual auth?
[08:18] Jordan: yes TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for syslog/HTTP ingestion are available. we can provision certificates or you can present one.
[08:28] Alex: great. action wrap: samira will share logs trimmed and schema, jordan will send SOC2 scoping, marcus will validate SSO metadata and provide a test user.
[08:38] Samira: i'll also include the batching tradeoff table and suggested settings for low-latency endpoints.
[08:45] Marcus: i'll aim to have SSO metadata and a test user by monday.
[08:49] Priya: and i'll review the SOC2 checklist when it's shared.
[08:53] Jordan: noted. anything else on compliance?
[08:57] Alex: one last thing — do you offer data residency in eu region? some of our data must stay in eu.
[09:05] Samira: yes, we can pin tenancy to eu-hosted regions on Dedicated or Private; hosted accounts can be region-pinned on request for enterprise plans.
[09:17] Marcus: what's the timeline for switching to a dedicated environment for performance tests?
[09:21] Samira: we can provision a dedicated pool for you in 2-3 weeks assuming contract sign-off; we can do an interim perf bench on the hosted stack if you want earlier.
[09:34] Alex: let's plan the hosted bench first then revisit dedicated if numbers look good.
[09:38] Jordan: sounds good. i'll recap in an email with the attachments and next steps.
[09:44] Priya: thanks all.
[09:46] Jordan: thanks, closing out.

Meeting close.
